newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to consider asking France for extraditions.
newsitem.headline: Spain to consider asking France for extraditions.

text.p: Spain's cabinet will consider on Friday asking France to extradite Jose Luis Urrusolo Sistiaga, the presumed number three in the separatist group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) who was detained last month, officials said.

The government will also discuss repeating previous requests to its northern neighbour for the extradition of two other suspected ETA guerrillas, Julian "Pototo" Atxurra Egurola and Carmen Guisasola Solozabal.

"The subject of the three extraditions will be discussed but we have to wait and see if the cabinet approves the request," an official in Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's office told Reuters on Thursday.

Urrusolo, 37, was picked up on January 17 in southern France and is one of Spain's most wanted men. He is suspected of being in charge of training commandos for ETA and of involvement in a number of killings and kidnappings over the past two decades.
There is a warrant for his arrest in Spain for killing two military officers in Barcelona in January 1992.

Egurola is believed to have been one of ETA's three top leaders and was said to have been in charge of logistics for ETA. He was captured in France last July and jailed for three years last October on conspiracy charges.
A French court last week set a hearing for March 5 on the extradition to Spain of several top ETA guerrillas including Egurola.
Spain has already asked five times for his extradition and has issued various warrants for his arrest on charges of killing policemen and staging bomb attacks.
Solozabal is serving a prison sentence in France for possession of illegal arms and is wanted in Spain for links to ETA and murder.
